figures.caption: Figure 5. Modeled specific electrical conductivity and specific number of conductive paths as a function of the amount of CB for the simulated electrode structures. to 10 wt % implies an electrical conductivity increase of about 18.65 %. The formation of conductive paths throughout the electrode causes the initial steep increase in conductivity. Once the amount of CB is sufficient to complete the conductive net- work path within the structure, the increase in conductivity is much slower because it simply implies an increment in the number of networks. This event is known in the literature as the percolation transition and has been commonly observed in various fields of research [47–49]. In order to analyze the electrode structures in more detail, the specific number of conductive paths within each structure was also examined.
